title: MLINE-referenced simple LTYPE with one binary XDATA chunk

scope.source: Runtime-generated LTYPE and APPID records; no repository drawing fixture is used or added.
scope.cross_product: Both source encodings were exported to both output encodings.
scope.linetype: EditDash, two simple dash segments [1.0, -0.5], declared length 1.5, source flags 0, alignment 65.

authority.relevant_rule: XDATA group 1004 carries binary data in chunks of at most 127 bytes; ASCII DXF represents those bytes as hexadecimal digits. This receipt tests one eight-byte chunk.

proof.source: Physical source fields and fresh import verify the exact APPID and 1004 hex chunk. Import-time origin, raw/typed equality, the AppIdName role and APPID name lookup bind the provider.
proof.output: The staged output proof checks exact 1001/1004 order and hex bytes in ASCII and binary DXF, APPID row common fields/flags/emitted owner and fresh typed readback of the chunk.
proof.failure_retry: Removing the source APPID provider refuses export and preserves the destination sentinel; restoring it succeeds on the same adapter. A late APPID-name mutation also refuses atomically and succeeds after correction on the same adapter.

limits: This receipt qualifies one eight-byte, uppercase-hex 1004 string chunk under one APPID. It does not qualify multi-chunk ordering, the 127-byte boundary, malformed hex/length refusal for this LTYPE schema, other XDATA values/orders, 1003/1005 dependency roles, coordinate tuples, APPID metadata, other LTYPE schemas or versions.
The receipt establishes transport only. It does not establish application-specific XDATA meaning, MLINE rendering, recursive document closure, or broader LTYPE provider support.
